Report of the Finance Department
To the Town of Hampton:
The Finance Department prepares and analyzes financial statements which are presented to
the Select Board monthly. Some of the other tasks that we complete during the year are assisting
with budget preparation, managing financial audit, cash reconciliation, preparing accounts
payable/receivables, process payroll, preparing municipal reports, and submitting for grant
reimbursements.
In 2024 the Finance Department continued to learn the new financial software that was
implemented in November of 2023. Change is always hard, but my team really embraced the
new system, and it has been a success so far.
The 2024 unaudited (current year) Income/Expense reports follow the format used when
reporting to the Select Board each month and open with a Financial Summary for the year.
Looking at revenues you will see that we took in $11,470,717 in revenue from sources such

government accounting, fund balance is the difference between assets and liabilities resulting in

a surplus or a deficit. A common misconception is that fund balance is a cash account, associated
with or correlated to a government’s bank account balance. But unlike a personal bank account,
a general fund balance is not a “cash-account;” it is a measure of equity between revenues and
expenditures. In the private sector it would be defined as a company’s working capital, but in
the public sector, it is referred to as fund balance. In government finance, the retention and use
of unassigned fund balance assists in measuring the financial health of an individual fund, such
as the general fund. The 2023 audited Unassigned Fund balance was $7,839,387.
In March of 2024, the voters passed warrant articles using Unassigned Fund Balance totaling
$1,154,500. At the time of setting the tax rate the Select Board used $500,000 to help reduce

Fund Balance as of December 31, 2024, is estimated to be $8,534,893. The official Unassigned
Fund Balance figure will come from the 2024 audit.
The Finance Director is also responsible for overseeing the MIS Team. The department
consists of 2 full-time and 1 part-time employee. These three employees are responsible for the
entire town network/computer system. This includes Town Hall, Recreation, DPW, Fire, Police
and Cemetery. They assist with elections and Channel 22 operations as well. The work that
they do to keep everything up and running is outstanding.
I would like to sincerely thank all my staff in Finance, MIS and Channel 22 for their
continued dedication to the Town. This group of employees goes above and beyond every day
and I am grateful to each of them.
The Finance Department and MIS look forward to another successful year in 2025 and
thank all the residents of Hampton for their continued support.
Respectfully submitted,
Kristi Pulliam
Finance Director

 The equation for determining the local property tax rate is as follows
 VOTED APPROPRIATIONS minus 
ALL OTHER REVENUE (not property taxes) x 1,000 
 TOTAL HAMPTON ASSESSED PROPERTY VALUE 
 Tax Rates
 The town tax rate is calculated by dividing the appropriations ( minus all revenue other than tax dollars) approved by the voters by the total assessed value of all taxable property (less total exemptions) in the Town. 
 The taxation process requires the cooperation of several divisions of the Town government. The Assessor estimates the value of your property. The town's people vote to determine the Town budget and school budget (aka appropriations), the County budget is set by the County Delegation, and the Hampton Beach Village District budget is set by their voters. 
 Once the tax rate has been set, the assessed value of your property is used to determine your portion of the tax levy. Divide your assessed value by 1,000, then multiply by the tax rate to determine your tax bill. The tax rate is expressed in terms of dollars per thousand or mill rate .
 Fair Assessment 
 It's the Assessor's job to discover, list and estimate the value of all properties within the jurisdiction of the Town. To ensure that all properties are treated uniformly, the Assessor's procedures must conform to State laws dealing with property taxation. Furthermore, commonly accepted appraisal and accounting practices must be used to determine:
 That the level of assessments and uniformity of assessments are within the acceptable ranges as recommended by the Assessing Standards Board.
 That assessment practices substantially comply with applicable statutes and rules.
 That the exemption and credit procedures substantially comply with applicable statutes and rules.
 That assessments are based on reasonably accurate data.
 That assessments of various types of properties are reasonably proportional to other types of property within the municipality.
 Revaluations
 In 2024 Hampton completed a revaluation of all properties within the community which resulted in the implementation of updated assessments that reflect a valuation date as of April 1, 2024. The Assessing office has been proactive in visiting and verifying all sales properties, new construction, and building permits which include the process of verifying all existing information including interior and exterior data. This allows the assessing office to ensure that both the physical and factual data is accurate. This will help promote fair and equitable assessments for everyone which is our ultimate goal.
 In addition, each year between revaluation cycles, the Assessor's office has to comply with the requirements of RSA 75:8 - Revised Inventory. This requires the assessing office to annually update assessments in accordance with State assessing guidelines, The Selectmen shall adjust assessments to reflect changes so that all assessments are reasonably proportional within the municipality .
 Adjustment of an Assessment 
 Assessors and Selectmen shall consider adjusting assessments for any properties that:
 They know or believe to have had a material physical change
 Changed ownership
 Have undergone zoning changes
 Have undergone subdivision, boundary line adjustments, or mergers
 Have undergone other changes affecting the value
 Geographic Information System Manager & Vision Online Database
 The Assessing website features access to Hampton's online Geographic Information System ( GIS ) Manager ; this site allows Hampton to share its parcel data with property owners, real estate professionals and other members of the community to query, browse, report and print maps including a full list of overlay maps, abutter lists and property information including a link to Vision's online assessment database all from their own computers.
 The Vision online database allows you to view the assessing data of all properties located within the Town. Just a reminder that the online database is updated monthly, so you may want to verify any recent sale or ownership information with the assessing office as our information is the official and the most current data available.

“Solid Waste Recusal Issue:
In my opinion, the Select Board should not require Selectman Rage to recuse himself from the
solid waste deliberations and votes for the following reasons:
1. Although the establishment of a cost recovery process for commercial trash and recycling
pickup will impact Selectman Rage's businesses, it will affect all businesses in the
commercial trash collection district. Some will be impacted more than Selectman Rage;
some will be affected less. Selectman Rage will not obtain a benefit that is unique to him,
his family, or his businesses. All members of the Board are Hampton taxpayers and will
be personally impacted by the decision, yea or nay, to establish a cost recovery process.
2. Selectman Rage has been open and forthcoming about his interest in this topic and his
desire to represent the interests of the Hampton Beach business community. This is no
surprise, and he does not wield any special powers as one of five members of the Select

the queue so UNH Extension is aware Hampton would be interested in applying, as they are
determining which towns are interested in participating and how to allocate their funding.
It was the consensus of the Select Board to have the Planning Board indicate the Town's interest in
the program to UNH Extension;
ECONOMIC & COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT SUMMIT: Ms. Mullen explained that earlier
this year Nate Bernitz from UNH Extension gave a presentation to the Planning Board on strategies
for business retention, expansion, and relationship building. The idea for a summit came out of that
presentation, an opportunity to engage with the business and developer community and to listen and
learn.
Mr. Bachand noted this summit could be geared towards those in the business community that did not
participate in the Charrette. He explained that the Planning Office is applying for an additional
Housing Opportunity Planning (HOP) Grant from InvestNH that is open to Housing Champion

PDF page 3
HAMPTON SELECT BOARD/ PLANNING BOARD
July 13, 2026-3:00 PM
designated communities. This grant ($1,000 - $5,000 range) is geared towards supporting active
efforts related to local housing. The Planning Office developed the idea of using this grant, if
awarded, for a Housing and Economic Development Summit in 2027. Mr. Bachand and Ms.
Novotney met with Jenn Rowden from the Rockingham Planning Commission last week to discuss
the idea with her.
The Boards discussed potential economic development goals.
It was the consensus of the Select Board to move forward with the proposed Housing and Economic
Development Summit.
ZONING UPDATES: Mr. Bachand explained that the first update will be to the definitions section
of the Zoning Ordinance. Making sure that definitions are compiled in the definitions section or
noted under which specific Section the definition can be found, that terms are defined once and
consistent with state law, and that conditions or standards are removed from all definitions whenever
possible. Also, every use in Section 5.1 should be defined in Section 1.5. This work will be done by
the Planning Office.
Mr. Bachand recommended the next update be a build out analysis. This was recommended by
Horsley Witten during the Zoning Audit as a guide for certain policy decisions.
Dimensional requirements analysis: A GIS exercise to compare the dimensional requirements in the
Zoning Ordinance with the actual requirements of lots and development today. The data should be
analyzed to see where there is significant mismatch. One of the goals of the Master Plan is to reduce
non-conformity based on dimensional requirements.
Suitability for greater housing density analysis: A GIS exercise to identify suitable areas for greater
housing density, in conjunction with the dimensional requirements analysis.
The cost for the build-out analysis would most likely need to be a Warrant Article. The remaining
HOP Grant would not be enough to cover the cost.
ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT COMMITTEE (EDC): Ms. Mullen stated this proposed
committee would be made up of professionals in the field willing to volunteer their expertise to the
Town. This committee would report to the Select Board. The EDC and the CBE would be separate
committees but would work together.
Ms. Hansen requested clarification on the mission of the proposed EDC. Ms. Mullen discussed
economic and community resilience. The other Planning Board members discussed their goals for an
EDC:
• Retaining current businesses, what is necessary to make them successful.
• Expanding current businesses.
• Attracting new business.
• Developing a non-residential tax base.
• Performing a SWOT (strength, weaknesses, opportunities, threats) analysis.
• Bringing recommendations to the community at large.
• How can the Town become more business aware.

PDF page 4
HAMPTON SELECT BOARD/ PLANNING BOARD
July 13, 2026 - 3:00 PM
Mr. Bliss proposed the name Economic Resilience Committee instead for a more holistic approach.
Ms. Novotney provided examples of EDCs working on public engagement and outreach for Town
projects that will have an impact on economic development. The Boards discussed looking at
examples of EDCs in other Towns.
RSA 79-E: Ms. Novotney noted that HB 1103 was approved on July 2nd and will go in effect on
August 31st. RSA 79-E:4-d will change its name from Office Conversion Zone to Residential
Conversion Zone. In a town that has adopted RSA 79-E:4-d a qualifying structure will now mean a
structure being used for office, commercial, or industrial use if such is being converted to residential
use. This will need to go to ballot in 2027 to make this change.
The Town can raise the substantial rehabilitation threshold, which is currently 15% of the pre-
rehabilitation assessed value or at least $75,000, whichever is less, but to do so it must go back to
ballot in 2027.
The Town may also amend the Public Benefit criteria but to do so it must also go back to ballot in
2027.
Ms. Novotney reviewed the draft RSA 79-E:4-d application and noted if the Board liked this
application format, it can be adjusted and used for the RSA 79-E application. Examples of the
proforma and project budget sheet used in the Lebanon RSA 79-E application, two Declaration of
Covenant templates (Milford and Rochester), examples of modified Public Benefits (Keene and
Durham), and proposed changes to the Hampton Public Benefits were provided.
The Boards discussed the RSA 79-E process. It was the consensus of the Select Board to have Mr.
Grip, Mr. Pope, and Ms. Novotney work on:
• Addressing the substantial rehabilitation threshold
• Drafting the modified Public Benefits
• Drafting a Covenant Template
• Creating a financial review process
ADJOURNMENT
MOVED by Mr. Lessard
SECOND by Mr. Grip
VOTE: Unanimous MOTION PASSED.
MEETING ADJOURNED: 4:51 p.m.
Respectfully submitted,
Andrea Novotney, Office Manager Planning

, we had a meeting with Executive Councilor Janet
Stevens, DOT Commissioner David Rodrigue, Select Board member Amy Hansen, Alex
Loiseau from the Hampton Beach Area Commission and Town Manager Sullivan. Everyone
agreed that lighting should be added to the bridge for security; the Board now needs to decide
whether to request pedestrian-only lighting or both pedestrian and roadway lights, we need to
send a letter to DOT as soon as possible indicating our preference; we need to decide what
kind of lights, and then DOT will give us options.

were: DOT will cover the cost of installing lights on the bridge, ongoing maintenance and
operation costs will need to be decided later, falling to either the state or the town; pros and
cons of each lighting type were discussed; installation will take at least a year; maintenance is
a major issue: the town does not have the equipment or staff to service lights; federal funds
can pay for installation but not long-term upkeep; the state has not shown interest in
maintaining the lights; members agree pedestrian lighting is essential for safety due to the
bridge’s height and windy conditions, members prefer full roadway and pedestrian lighting for
maximum security; DOT requires a formal request specifying which type the town wants.

The meeting/tour started at 9:30 a.m. at the Hampton Fire Department 140 Winnacunnet Rd.
The Committee met with Chief McMahon and Deputy Chief Nathan Denio. The discussion
initially focused on fire station maintenance needs at both the main station and the beach sub-
station. Chief McMahon spoke to his budget, noting that 88% is allocated to personnel costs,
with the remaining 12% covering all other expenses, including, but not limited to, building
maintenance, training, computer software, utilities, and fuel. He discussed the challenges of
making necessary building repairs during a default budget year. The department is currently fully
staffed, although four staff members are out for various reasons. The cost of training tuition and
class fees has increased. The overtime budget is underfunded, as the department must ensure
adequate coverage regardless of the reason for an employee’s absence, including sick leave,
vacation, military obligations, and workers’ compensation.
A question was asked about when a new ambulance will be required and the expected lifespan of
an ambulance. The cost of ambulances comes out of the EMS fund, which is funded through
insurance billing when an ambulance and its team provide services. Ambulance purchases are
staggered. The next purchase is targeted for 2027, with delivery expected in 2028. The lifespan
of an ambulance is approximately eight years.
The ladder truck that voters approved this year has been ordered and came in below expectations
in terms of cost. It is expected to be delivered in 2028.
The Committee toured the EMS training lab, where staff practice and improve their skills in
providing advanced lifesaving procedures.

§ 718-1. Authority.
In accordance with the provisions of RSA 41:8, 41:9 and 37:6 the Board of Selectmen and the
Town Manager hereby adopt the following purchasing procedures that govern the purchase of
supplies, materials, and services, to implement the Purchasing Policy of the Town of Hampton.
1. Editor’s Note: This ordinance superseded former Ch. 718, Purchasing Policy and Purchasing Procedures, adopted 6-18-2012.

§ 718-2 HAMPTON CODE § 718-4
§ 718-2. Purpose.
It is the intent and purpose of this policy to establish uniform purchasing procedures for the
Town of Hampton to protect the public welfare and to assure fair and equitable treatment in
the purchasing of supplies, materials, and services as contained in the purchasing procedures
of the Town.
§ 718-3. Purchase of Supplies, Materials, and Services l e s s t h a n $ 5 , 0 0 0 .
A. T he Town Manager and the department heads that report to the Town Manager who have
appropriations approved by the Town Meeting, and/or those who have authority to expend
funds from expendable special accounts created in accordance with applicable laws can
authorize the expenditure of funds when the sums to be expended do not exceed $5,000 for
any one purpose.
(1) The department heads or the chair or other designated members of a department, board,
committee or commission that does not report to the Board of Selectmen or the Town
Manager that have appropriations approved by Town Meeting and/or those who have
authority to expend funds from applicable special accounts created in accordance with
applicable laws, and whose bills are paid through the Finance Department can authorize
the expenditure of funds when the sum to be expended does not exceed $5,000 for any
purpose.
(2) Departments should exercise due diligence in making all purchases, including those
under $5,000, by obtaining three verbal or written quotes to ensure the best value for
the Town, unless sole source is necessary or in cases where it is not possible to find
three vendors due to the specialty of supplies, materials, or services.
§ 718-4. Purchase Requisition Required for Expenditures between $5,000 and $49,999.
All purchases for supplies, materials, and services that exceed a value of $5,000 (but are less
than $50,000,) shall require a properly signed and executed purchase requisition in advance of
the acquisition of the supplies, materials, or services procured unless otherwise excepted
herein.
A. Purchase requisitions for the following items are not required:
(1) Utility bills

Purchases that require a requisition must obtain the signature of the Town Manager, or in
his or her absence, the Acting Town Manager (in the absence of the Town Manager and
the Acting Town Manager the Finance Director may sign purchase requisitions,) prior to
the materials, products, or services being ordered.
No supplies, materials or services shall be purchased, ordered, or received by any officer,
department head, or employee of the Town without first obtaining a minimum of three (3)
written quotes. The Department Head, or their designee, shall contact as many vendors as
necessary in order to obtain at least three (3) written quotations for each different item
being purchased. Documentation of internet-based pricing is considered a written quote
for the purposes of this policy.
§ 718-5. Contents of Purchase Requisitions.
P u r c h a s e r e q u i s i t i o n s s h a l l b e completed before the ordering or purchasing of supplies,
materials and services, and shall, at a minimum, contain the following information: the name
and address of the vendor; the name and address of the purchasing department; the account
code(s); the location to which the supplies, or materials are to be shipped or delivered; the
quantity to be purchased; a description of the supplies; materials or services to be purchased;
including any shipping expense and/or delivery costs (note that the costs need not be exact if
unknown but an estimated amount must be supplied by the vendor); the date issued; and the
authorized or required signature(s).
Departments shall use the Purchase Requisition Form authorized by the Finance Department.
§ 718-6. Purchase Requisition Distribution.
Purchase requisitions, following their completion and signing shall be distributed as follows:
the original to remain in Finance, a copy to be retained by the issuing department, and a copy
forwarded to vendor, if requested.
§ 718-7. Expiration of Purchase Requisition.
Purchase requisitions once issued are valid until the expiration of the fiscal year of their
issuance.

§ 718-8 HAMPTON CODE § 718-9
§ 718–8. Purchase of Supplies, Materials, and Services over $50,000.
A. All purchases of supplies, materials, and services, the cost of which is estimated to exceed
$50,000 shall be allowed only after competitive sealed bids or sealed written professional
proposals have been solicited. Excluded from this requirement are legal, engineering, and
architectural services.
B. Legal, Engineering and Architectural Services: The procurement of services from
attorneys, engineers and architects shall be based upon their competency, qualifications
and experience as determined through a qualification - based selection (QBS) process
utilizing requests for qualifications (RFQ) and other processes that result in the selection
of the most advantageous provider to the Town of Hampton. The issuance of any RFQ's
for the procurement of these services shall have prior authorization and approval of the
Town Manager.
C. Town Departments, Boards, Commissions, and Committees shall solicit sealed bids and
professional proposals in such a manner that the prepared documents do not contain
restrictive or proprietary language unless they are qualified by using terminology that will
permit the substitution of comparable supplies, materials, and services that will achieve
the same goals and objectives regardless of the substitution.
D. The above notwithstanding, sole source of supply, service or item may be warranted in
certain limited circumstances. Such procurement by sole source should only be authorized
by the Department Head, and should be based on the needs of the community, not as a
means of avoiding competitive proposals or bids. The reasons for such sole source activity
must be well documented.
E. Items that are purchased via State or Federal Bids (which must be thoroughly documented)
are excluded from the bidding or requisition requirements, as are any items waived by the
Town Manager or items that are specifically voted under a Town Meeting Warrant Article
that directs that a specific vendor be used for a specific purchase.
§ 718-9. Bid Process
A. Departments, Boards, Committees, or Commissions may contact the Town Manager’s
Administrative Assistant for required formats prior to preparing written documents that
conform with the Purchasing Policy.
B. Draft bids or proposals may be referred to Town Counsel for legal review, if necessary.
Upon completion, bids or proposals shall be sent to the designated prospective bidders.

the posting of security, by bond or otherwise, in an amount at least equal to 100% of the
contract price, conditioned upon the payment by the contractors and subcontractors for all

D. Once bid documents or proposals are completed, they are to be forwarded electronically to
the Administrative Assistant in the Town Manager's Office. Accompanying the bid
documents will be the list of prospective bidders prepared by the bidding entity.
§ 7 1 8 - 1 0 . N o t i c e o f B i d o r P r o p o s a l .
An invitation to bid or request for proposals shall be publicly announced by placing the bid or
proposal documents on the Town' s website, and by sending invitations to bid and requests for
proposals directly to potential bidders and proposers, and forwarding such invitations or
requests to construction advertising agencies, association websites, etc. When appropriate the
Town may utilize newspaper advertisements to announce invitations to bid and requests for
proposals.
§ 7 1 8 - 1 1 . A w a r d o f B i d s o r P r o f e s s i o n a l P r o p o s a l s .
All sealed bids or written professional proposals shall be awarded by the Town Manager on
the following basis:
A. Sealed bids and professional proposals shall be awarded to the lowest responsible bidder
or proposer except that, in addition to price, the following shall be considered:
(1) The ability, capacity, and skill of the bidder or proposer, through the submission of
required information as a portion of the bid or proposal, to perform the contract or
provide the services required and the qualifications of personnel who will be involved
in any work to be performed.
(2) Whether the bidder or proposer can perform the contract or provide the service(s)
required by the terms of the bid or proposal promptly, or within the time specified,
without delay or interference.

§ 718-11 HAMPTON CODE § 718-15
(4) The quality, performance, timeliness, completeness and cost containment of previous
contracts or services for the Town or others.
B. When bids or proposals are received, the department head will document the results of the
bid or proposal and forward the documentation to the Town Manager together with a
statement either that the purchase complies with the purchasing policy or, that the purchase
does not comply with the purchasing policy, and therefore requires a waiver voted by the
Board of Selectmen or Town Manager, as appropriate, before action can be taken by a
department to purchase.
§ 718-12. Right to Accept or Reject Bids and Proposals.
The Town, acting through the Town Manager, reserves to itself the exclusive right to reject or
accept any or all bids or proposals received as determined by the Town Manager to be in the
best interests of the Town.
§ 7 1 8 - 1 3 . B i d s a n d P r o p o s a l s t o C o m p l y W i t h o u t M o d i f i c a t i o n .
A. To be accepted, the bid(s) or proposal(s) must, as initially submitted, constitute a complete,
unqualified offer that includes all the material terms of the invitations for bid(s) or
professional proposal(s) or solicitation(s) and provides all the terms for the contract,
without further modification, for the supplies, materials, or services solicited.
B. This section shall not be operative where an invitation to bid or a request for a proposal
specifically allows for the bidder or proposer to provide alternative bids or proposals or
changes in specifications. Such inoperability under this section shall be permitted only
where specifically shown in any bid or proposal solicitation, but not otherwise.
§ 718-14. Control, Supervision and Enforcement.
The provisions of this policy shall be subject to control, supervision, and enforcement by the
Town Manager.
§ 718-15. Signature Required.
The signature(s) of the Town Manager under RSA 37:6 shall be required to award a bid or
professional proposal hereunder.
718:6 07-25-2022

PDF page 7
§ 718-16 PURCHASING POLICY AND PROCEDURES § 718-20
§ 718-16. Exceptions to Public Bidding or Professional Proposal Requirements.
The requirement for public bidding or written professional proposals may be excepted where
it can be demonstrated to the Town Manager’s satisfaction that the particular supply, material
or service can only be provided by a single source supplier or when the Town Meeting
specifically votes to purchase a particular supply, material or service from a specific provider
and no other or when there is a declared public emergency that requires immediate action to
procure a particular supply, material or service.
§ 718-17. Emergencies.
When the public health and welfare, because of a declared public emergency, requires the
immediate purchase of supplies, materials, or services, the Town Manager or individual
department head or individual boards, committees, or commissions responsible for emergency
services shall have authority to purchase needed supplies, materials, and services to meet the
needs of the public emergency without the necessity of obtaining approved purchase
requisitions. In such cases, purchase requisitions shall be completed following the emergency,
if they are for purchases over the dollar thresholds outlined in this policy.
§ 718-18. Policy Waivers
The Board of Selectmen may by vote, grant a waiver from the provisions of this policy, if they
find that the waiver that is to be granted is in the best interests of the Town of Hampton, and is
in the spirit of this policy.
§ 718-19. Repeal and Applicability.
The adoption of this policy automatically repeals any and all past policies or practices that
may have been or currently are in force but does not apply retroactively to purchases already
agreed to on behalf of the Town.
§ 718-20. When Effective.
This policy shall become effective upon its adoption by the Board of Selectmen.
